title: Exploring the Development Project Structure
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of exploring the development project structure.
Apply one appropriate technique to a small Tailwind CSS example.
Verify the expected result and identify a common failure mode.

content.intro: In this lesson, focus on exploring the development project structure and connect it to the way Tailwind CSS generates and applies utility styles.
content.why_it_matters: A repeatable setup for exploring the development project structure prevents version and build-tool mismatches that can make valid utilities appear not to work.

content_blocks.title: Module 3 learning map
content_blocks.alt_text: Four-step module learning map: Choosing a Tailwind CSS Development Setup → Installing Tailwind CSS with the CLI → Exploring the Development Project Structure → Creating Your First Tailwind CSS Page. Lesson pages add code examples and practice.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The source curriculum highlights: HTML and component source files; CSS entry files; Package configuration; Build configuration; Public assets and generated output. Treat these as practical decisions rather than a list to memorize: identify the intended behavior, choose the smallest suitable utility or directive, and inspect what the browser receives.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with the example, change one decision related to exploring the development project structure, then compare the outcome. In a Tailwind-enabled project, confirm the generated CSS exists; class strings alone do not make styles available without a configured build.

content_blocks.title: Version and compatibility note
content_blocks.text: This course prioritizes Tailwind CSS v4. Confirm your installed version and use its matching official guide. Snippets using v3 directives or configuration are labelled as legacy and should not be mixed blindly with v4 syntax.

content.task: Create a minimal example demonstrating exploring the development project structure. Include a before/after comparison and explain why the chosen utility, variant or directive is appropriate.
task_acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate at least one decision tied to exploring the development project structure.
Keep the example easy to inspect, with complete utility names.
Test the outcome and document one limitation or environment assumption.
hints: Identify which listed syllabus topic is most important to exploring the development project structure.
Change one utility, token, variant or configuration setting at a time.
Inspect generated CSS and computed styles before changing unrelated code.
content.expected_output: A centered content section with a prominent heading and readable paragraph; rendering requires the configured Tailwind build.
troubleshooting: If no style appears, verify the package, CSS import and build-tool integration before changing the HTML.
If only a state or breakpoint style fails, check the full class token, source detection, condition and computed CSS.
For a framework snippet, import the stylesheet through its supported entry point and consult the current official guide.
common_mistakes: Applying exploring the development project structure without checking generated styles or browser behavior.
Mixing Tailwind v3 and v4 setup examples without a migration plan.
Treating visual appearance as a substitute for semantic markup, keyboard usability or actual component behavior.
summary: Exploring the Development Project Structure is one part of a predictable utility-first styling workflow.
Keep examples small, test the built interface and use version-matched documentation.
